## Introduction

The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they're already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.

### Objective

The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
phases

_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_

## Requirements

### Frontend

The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
and CSS.

### Backend

The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.

### Database

Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a
SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.


## Structure

### Login

```
The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages
should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page
```
### Navigation

```
The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added
pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly
```
#### Common Layout

```
The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login
pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and
industry-standard look.
The Setting Page should be accessible from the same pages but via a profile icon in
the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar
```
### Landing Page

```
The Landing Page should be a simple page with the Navigation Bar and Profile Icon
and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use
the database to retrieve the user's name and include it in the welcome message to
make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that
function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar
```
### Dashboard

```
The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with
dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The
dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team
should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here
(Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should
include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns
of API calls by page.
```

### Audit Log

```
The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information
about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the
actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This
should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log
table in the database.
```
### Settings

```
The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their
own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the
page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone
number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally).
```
### 404 Page

```
The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or
Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request
```

    """
    Dependency function to get database session

    db = SessionLocal()

from datetime import datetime

class User(Base):
    """User model for authentication and user information"""
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    username = Column(String(50), unique=True, index=True, nullable=False)

## Introduction

The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they're already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.

### Objective

The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
phases

_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_

## Requirements

### Frontend

The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
and CSS.

### Backend

The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.

### Database

Due to the limited resources and exploratory nature of the capstone, the team should use a
SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.


## Structure

### Login

```
The web-app should have basic login and authentication functionality. All pages
should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page
```
### Navigation

```
The web-app should have a styled navigation bar that stays up to date with added
pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly
```
#### Common Layout

```
The navigation bar should be persistent on all pages except the 404 and Login
pages. The bar should be responsive to different layouts and maintain a clean and
industry-standard look.
The Setting Page should be accessible from the same pages but via a profile icon in
the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar
```
### Landing Page

```
The Landing Page should be a simple page with the Navigation Bar and Profile Icon
and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use
the database to retrieve the user's name and include it in the welcome message to
make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that
function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar
```
### Dashboard

```
The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with
dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The
dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team
should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here
(Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should
include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns
of API calls by page.
```

### Audit Log

```
The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information
about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the
actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This
should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log
table in the database.
```
### Settings

```
The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their
own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the
page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone
number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally).
```
### 404 Page

```
The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or
Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request
```

def verify_password(plain_password: str, hashed_password: str) -> bool:
    """Verify a plain password against a hashed password"""
    return pwd_context.verify(plain_password, hashed_password)


def get_password_hash(password: str) -> str:
    """Hash a plain password"""
    return pwd_context.hash(password)


def authenticate_user(db: Session, username: str, password: str) -> Optional[User]:
    """
    Authenticate user with username and password.
    Returns user object if successful, None otherwise.
    """
    user = get_user_by_username(db, username)
    if not user:
        return None
    if not verify_password(password, user.hashed_password):
        return None
    return user


def create_access_token(data: dict, expires_delta: Optional[timedelta] = None) -> str:
    """Create a new JWT access token"""
    to_encode = data.copy()
    expire = datetime.utcnow() + (expires_delta or timedelta(minutes=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES))
    to_encode.update({"exp": expire})
    return jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)


def verify_token(token: str) -> dict:
    """

    Returns payload dict if valid, raises HTTPException otherwise.
    """
    credentials_exception = HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="Could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
        user_id: int = payload.get("sub")
        if user_id is None:
            raise credentials_exception
        return payload
    except JWTError:
        raise credentials_exception


def get_current_user(
    token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> User:
    """FastAPI dependency: get the current authenticated user from the JWT."""
    payload = verify_token(token)
    user_id = payload.get("sub")
    user = get_user_by_id(db, int(user_id))
    if user is None or not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="User not found or inactive",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    return user


def get_user_by_username(db: Session, username: str) -> Optional[User]:
    """Get user by username"""
    return db.query(User).filter(User.username == username).first()


def get_user_by_id(db: Session, user_id: int) -> Optional[User]:
    """Get user by ID"""
    return db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()

from database.models import AuditLog, User


def create_audit_log(
    db: Session,
    user_id: int,
    action: str,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    details: Optional[str] = None,
    ip_address: Optional[str] = None,
    user_agent: Optional[str] = None
) -> AuditLog:
    """Create a new audit log entry"""
    audit_log = AuditLog(
        user_id=user_id,
        action=action,
        description=description,
        details=details,
        ip_address=ip_address,
        user_agent=user_agent,
        timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
    )
    db.add(audit_log)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(audit_log)
    return audit_log


def get_audit_logs(
    db: Session,
    user_id: Optional[int] = None,
    page: int = 1,
    page_size: int = 20
) -> dict:
    """Get paginated audit log entries, newest first."""
    query = db.query(AuditLog)
    if user_id is not None:
        query = query.filter(AuditLog.user_id == user_id)

    total = query.count()
    total_pages = max(1, math.ceil(total / page_size))

    logs = (
        query
        .order_by(AuditLog.timestamp.desc())
        .offset((page - 1) * page_size)
        .limit(page_size)
        .all()
    )

    return {
        "data": logs,
        "total": total,
        "page": page,
        "page_size": page_size,
        "total_pages": total_pages,
    }


def get_audit_log_by_id(db: Session, log_id: int) -> Optional[AuditLog]:
    """Get a specific audit log entry by ID"""
    return db.query(AuditLog).filter(AuditLog.id == log_id).first()


def log_login(db: Session, user_id: int, ip_address: str, user_agent: str) -> AuditLog:

from datetime import datetime

from fastapi import Request
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.responses import Response
from typing import Callable
import time

from database.database import SessionLocal
from database.models import APIUsage


# Map URL prefixes to page names for API usage tracking
PAGE_PREFIX_MAP = {
    "/api/auth": "auth",
    "/api/landing": "landing",
    "/api/dashboard": "dashboard",
    "/api/audit": "audit",
    "/api/settings": "settings",
}


def _resolve_page(path: str) -> str:
    """Determine which logical page a request path belongs to."""
    for prefix, page in PAGE_PREFIX_MAP.items():
        if path.startswith(prefix):
            return page
    return "other"


class SecurityMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    """
    Middleware for:
    - Security headers
    - API usage tracking for dashboard statistics
    """

    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next: Callable) -> Response:
        start_time = time.time()

        response = await call_next(request)

        process_time = time.time() - start_time

        # Security headers
        response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
        response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
        response.headers["X-XSS-Protection"] = "1; mode=block"
        response.headers["Strict-Transport-Security"] = "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"

        # Track API usage for /api/* endpoints
        path = request.url.path
        if path.startswith("/api/"):
            try:
                db = SessionLocal()
                try:
                    usage = APIUsage(
                        endpoint=path,
                        method=request.method,
                        page=_resolve_page(path),
                        response_status=response.status_code,
                        response_time_ms=int(process_time * 1000),
                        timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
                    )
                    db.add(usage)
                    db.commit()
                finally:
                    db.close()
            except Exception:
                pass  # Don't let tracking errors break the request

        return response

@router.post("/login", response_model=LoginResponse)
async def login(body: LoginRequest, request: Request, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    """Authenticate user and return access token"""
    user = authenticate_user(db, body.username, body.password)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid username or password",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )

    access_token = create_access_token(
        data={"sub": str(user.id), "username": user.username},
        expires_delta=timedelta(minutes=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES),
    )

    # Audit log
    log_login(
        db,
        user_id=user.id,
        ip_address=request.client.host if request.client else "unknown",
        user_agent=request.headers.get("user-agent", "unknown"),
    )

    return LoginResponse(
        access_token=access_token,
        token_type="bearer",
        expires_in=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES * 60,
        user_id=user.id,
        username=user.username,
        name=user.name,
    )

async def logout(
    request: Request,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),

):

    log_logout(

        ip_address=request.client.host if request.client else "unknown",
        user_agent=request.headers.get("user-agent", "unknown"),

    body: TokenRefreshRequest,

    payload = verify_token(body.refresh_token)
    user_id = int(payload.get("sub"))
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
    if not user or not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Invalid token")

    new_token = create_access_token(
        data={"sub": str(user.id), "username": user.username},
        expires_delta=timedelta(minutes=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES),
    )
    return LoginResponse(
        access_token=new_token,
        token_type="bearer",
        expires_in=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES * 60,

def _default_dates(start_date, end_date):
    """Return sensible defaults when dates are omitted."""
    if end_date is None:
        end_date = date.today()
    if start_date is None:
        start_date = end_date - timedelta(days=30)
    return start_date, end_date


@router.get("/idms-data", response_model=IDMSDataListResponse)
async def get_idms_data(

    db: Session = Depends(get_db),

    rows = db.query(IDMSData).all()
    return IDMSDataListResponse(
        data=[IDMSDataResponse.model_validate(r) for r in rows],
        total=len(rows),
    )


@router.get("/api-usage", response_model=APIUsageStats)
async def get_api_usage(
    start_date: date = Query(None, description="Start date for filtering"),
    end_date: date = Query(None, description="End date for filtering"),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Get API usage statistics within a date range"""
    start_date, end_date = _default_dates(start_date, end_date)
    total = (
        db.query(func.count(APIUsage.id))
        .filter(func.date(APIUsage.timestamp) >= start_date)
        .filter(func.date(APIUsage.timestamp) <= end_date)
        .scalar()
    )
    return APIUsageStats(total_calls=total or 0, start_date=start_date, end_date=end_date)


@router.get("/api-usage/breakdown", response_model=APIUsageBreakdownResponse)
async def get_api_usage_breakdown(
    start_date: date = Query(None, description="Start date for filtering"),
    end_date: date = Query(None, description="End date for filtering"),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Get API usage breakdown by page"""
    start_date, end_date = _default_dates(start_date, end_date)

    rows = (
        db.query(APIUsage.page, func.count(APIUsage.id).label("count"))
        .filter(func.date(APIUsage.timestamp) >= start_date)
        .filter(func.date(APIUsage.timestamp) <= end_date)
        .group_by(APIUsage.page)
        .all()
    )
    total = sum(r.count for r in rows) or 1  # avoid division by zero
    breakdown = [
        APIUsageByPage(page=r.page, count=r.count, percentage=round(r.count / total * 100, 2))
        for r in rows
    ]
    return APIUsageBreakdownResponse(
        breakdown=breakdown,
        total_calls=sum(r.count for r in rows),
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, UploadFile, File

from database.database import get_db
from database.models import User
from schemas.user import UserUpdate, UserResponse, UserPasswordUpdate
from services.auth_service import get_current_user, verify_password, get_password_hash

from config import UPLOAD_DIR, MAX_FILE_SIZE, ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/", response_model=UserResponse)
async def get_user_settings(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    """Get current user settings"""
    return current_user


@router.put("/", response_model=UserResponse)
async def update_user_settings(
    body: UserUpdate,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Update user settings (name, username, email, phone)"""
    updated_fields = []
    update_data = body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)

    for field, value in update_data.items():
        if value is not None and getattr(current_user, field) != value:
            # Check uniqueness for username/email
            if field == "username":
                existing = db.query(User).filter(User.username == value, User.id != current_user.id).first()
                if existing:
                    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Username already taken")
            if field == "email":
                existing = db.query(User).filter(User.email == value, User.id != current_user.id).first()
                if existing:
                    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Email already taken")
            setattr(current_user, field, value)
            updated_fields.append(field)

    if updated_fields:
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(current_user)
        log_profile_update(db, current_user.id, updated_fields)

    return current_user


@router.put("/password")
async def update_password(
    body: UserPasswordUpdate,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Update user password"""
    if not verify_password(body.current_password, current_user.hashed_password):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Current password is incorrect")

    if body.new_password != body.confirm_password:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="New passwords do not match")

    if len(body.new_password) < 8:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="New password must be at least 8 characters")

    current_user.hashed_password = get_password_hash(body.new_password)
    db.commit()

    log_password_change(db, current_user.id)

    return {"message": "Password updated successfully"}


@router.post("/profile-picture", response_model=UserResponse)
async def upload_profile_picture(
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Upload new profile picture"""
    # Validate extension
    ext = file.filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in file.filename else ""
    if ext not in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=f"File type not allowed. Allowed: {', '.join(ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS)}",
        )

    # Read and validate size
    contents = await file.read()
    if len(contents) > MAX_FILE_SIZE:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="File too large. Maximum size is 5MB")

    # Save file
    os.makedirs(UPLOAD_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    filename = f"{current_user.id}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}.{ext}"
    filepath = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, filename)
    with open(filepath, "wb") as f:
        f.write(contents)

    # Delete old picture if exists
    if current_user.profile_picture:
        old_path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, current_user.profile_picture)
        if os.path.exists(old_path):
            os.remove(old_path)

    current_user.profile_picture = filename
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(current_user)

    log_profile_update(db, current_user.id, ["profile_picture"])

    return current_user


@router.delete("/profile-picture")
async def delete_profile_picture(
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Delete current profile picture"""
    if current_user.profile_picture:
        old_path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, current_user.profile_picture)
        if os.path.exists(old_path):
            os.remove(old_path)
        current_user.profile_picture = None
        db.commit()
        log_profile_update(db, current_user.id, ["profile_picture"])

    return {"message": "Profile picture removed"}

import os
import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, UploadFile, File
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from database.database import get_db
from database.models import User
from schemas.user import UserUpdate, UserResponse, UserPasswordUpdate
from services.auth_service import get_current_user, verify_password, get_password_hash
from services.audit_service import log_profile_update, log_password_change
from config import UPLOAD_DIR, MAX_FILE_SIZE, ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/", response_model=UserResponse)
async def get_user_settings(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    """Get current user settings"""
    return current_user


@router.put("/", response_model=UserResponse)
async def update_user_settings(
    body: UserUpdate,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Update user settings (name, username, email, phone)"""
    updated_fields = []
    update_data = body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)

    for field, value in update_data.items():
        if value is not None and getattr(current_user, field) != value:
            # Check uniqueness for username/email
            if field == "username":
                existing = db.query(User).filter(User.username == value, User.id != current_user.id).first()
                if existing:
                    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Username already taken")
            if field == "email":
                existing = db.query(User).filter(User.email == value, User.id != current_user.id).first()
                if existing:
                    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Email already taken")
            setattr(current_user, field, value)
            updated_fields.append(field)

    if updated_fields:
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(current_user)
        log_profile_update(db, current_user.id, updated_fields)

    return current_user


@router.put("/password")
async def update_password(
    body: UserPasswordUpdate,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Update user password"""
    if not verify_password(body.current_password, current_user.hashed_password):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Current password is incorrect")

    if body.new_password != body.confirm_password:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="New passwords do not match")

    if len(body.new_password) < 8:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="New password must be at least 8 characters")

    current_user.hashed_password = get_password_hash(body.new_password)
    db.commit()

    log_password_change(db, current_user.id)

    return {"message": "Password updated successfully"}


@router.post("/profile-picture", response_model=UserResponse)
async def upload_profile_picture(
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Upload new profile picture"""
    # Validate extension
    ext = file.filename.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in file.filename else ""
    if ext not in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=f"File type not allowed. Allowed: {', '.join(ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS)}",
        )

    # Read and validate size
    contents = await file.read()
    if len(contents) > MAX_FILE_SIZE:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="File too large. Maximum size is 5MB")

    # Save file
    os.makedirs(UPLOAD_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    filename = f"{current_user.id}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}.{ext}"
    filepath = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, filename)
    with open(filepath, "wb") as f:
        f.write(contents)

    # Delete old picture if exists
    if current_user.profile_picture:
        old_path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, current_user.profile_picture)
        if os.path.exists(old_path):
            os.remove(old_path)

    current_user.profile_picture = filename
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(current_user)

    log_profile_update(db, current_user.id, ["profile_picture"])

    return current_user


@router.delete("/profile-picture")
async def delete_profile_picture(
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Delete current profile picture"""
    if current_user.profile_picture:
        old_path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, current_user.profile_picture)
        if os.path.exists(old_path):
            os.remove(old_path)
        current_user.profile_picture = None
        db.commit()
        log_profile_update(db, current_user.id, ["profile_picture"])

    return {"message": "Profile picture removed"}", "oldString": """"

1. **No `.env` file** — The app falls back to hardcoded defaults (e.g. `SECRET_KEY = "your-secret-key-change-in-production"`). A `.env` file with a real secret key should be created.

2. **No user registration endpoint** — There's a `UserCreate` schema in [backend/schemas/user.py](backend/schemas/user.py) but no `POST /api/auth/register` route. Users can only be created manually in the DB. If signup functionality is needed, a registration endpoint should be added.

S26 – MICHELIN X CLEMSON CAPSTONE REQ SHEET
The purpose of this capstone project is not for the Capstone Team to demonstrate or
improve their web app development skills, we have no doubt they’re already spectacular.
The point is to measure how long it takes a team of developers to build one website versus
how long it takes to build and use an agentic AI pipeline to do the same thing.
The first phase of this project is to build a traditional website meeting the requirements
specified below. For simplicity the website will be developed without any common
development frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) in favor of using raw HTML, JS, and CSS _*._
After the development finishes, the team will move to the AI pipeline development segment
of the project. Since we want to compare the length of time it takes for development to
complete there is not a strict schedule for the phases, but Michelin may adjust
requirements to ensure each phase is completed with enough time remaining for the other
_*This decision is meant to speed up the project under the assumption the team is more familiar with this type
of web development and can be retracted if this is not the case_
The frontend of the application should be consistent throughout the application and
similar to the design system used by Michelin (example mockups will be provided for
students to replicate for future screens). The frontend will be developed using HTML, JS,
The backend of the application will be a simple python Fast API server that runs locally. The
backend should be organized by screen and handle any required request from the frontend
and return industry standard formatted responses. The backend should also be configured
in a way that employs the proper security measures that protect it from injections, cross-
origin attacks, and other common pitfalls of web-app development.

SQLite, or a similar lightweight database that can be hosted locally along with the backend.

should check for valid authentication and if it is not found route to a login page that
validates credentials and issues an authentication token. A successful login should
route the user to the Landing Page

pages as the project develops. The navigation bar should correctly navigate users to
different pages and validate the user is authenticated and if not route them to the
Login Page. The navigation bar should be a collapsable menu and the various pages
of the app should react to this properly

the top-right corner rather than in the navigation bar

and a simple welcome message to the website. The welcome message should use
the database to retrieve the user’s name and include it in the welcome message to
make it more personal. The page should also give quick navigation links that
function the same as a tab in the Navigation Bar
The dashboard should pull data from a table in the IDMS that is populated with
dummy data. The page will feature a stylized table of certain columns. The
dashboard will also use a separate table that tracks API usage of the site. The team
should implement functionality to capture data on their backend API to display here
(Can be initialized with dummy data for development purposes). This data should
include the number of API calls made in a user selected date range and breakdowns
The Audit Log page is similar to the Dashboard. Its purpose is to show information
about recent activity the user has done. It should show a table showcasing the
actions performed by the user on the app sorted from most recent to oldest. This
should show things like logins and user info updates and be stored in an audit log
The settings page will be a stylized form that allows users to view and update their
own user information. User changes should be saved in the DB and reflected on the
page. User information should include name, username, password, email, phone
number, profile picture (A filename that is stored and retrieved locally).
The 404 page will be a stylized page that does not include the Navigation Bar or
Profile Icon that is loaded when users make an invalid API request

Shared test fixtures for the Michelin Capstone backend tests.

Uses an in-memory SQLite database so production data is never touched.
"""

import os
import sys

# Ensure the backend package root is on sys.path so bare imports like
# ``from config import …`` work the same way they do when running the app.
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

from database.database import Base, get_db
from database.models import User, AuditLog, APIUsage, IDMSData
from services.auth_service import get_password_hash, create_access_token

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In-memory database engine shared across each test function
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEST_DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///file::memory:?cache=shared"

engine = create_engine(TEST_DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)


def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App fixture — fresh tables for every test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.fixture()
def app():
    """Create all tables, yield the FastAPI app, then drop everything."""
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

    from main import app as _app
    _app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    yield _app
    _app.dependency_overrides.clear()

    Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)


@pytest.fixture()
def client(app):
    """TestClient bound to the test app."""
    return TestClient(app)


@pytest.fixture()
def db():
    """Raw database session for setting up test data."""
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()
        Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convenience helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.fixture()
def test_user(app) -> User:
    """Insert a test user and return the ORM object."""
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    user = User(
        username="testuser",
        email="test@example.com",
        name="Test User",
        phone="555-0100",
        hashed_password=get_password_hash("password123"),
        is_active=True,
    )
    session.add(user)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(user)
    session.close()
    return user


@pytest.fixture()
def auth_header(test_user) -> dict:
    """Return an Authorization header with a valid JWT for *test_user*."""
    token = create_access_token(data={"sub": str(test_user.id), "username": test_user.username})
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}


@pytest.fixture()
def second_user(app) -> User:
    """Insert a second user for access-control tests."""
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    user = User(
        username="other",
        email="other@example.com",
        name="Other User",
        hashed_password=get_password_hash("otherpass1"),
        is_active=True,
    )
    session.add(user)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(user)
    session.close()
    return user
"}

# ── Login ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_login_success(client, test_user):
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "password123"})
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["access_token"]
    assert data["token_type"] == "bearer"
    assert data["user_id"] == test_user.id
    assert data["username"] == "testuser"
    assert data["name"] == "Test User"
    assert data["expires_in"] > 0


def test_login_wrong_password(client, test_user):
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "wrong"})
    assert resp.status_code == 401


def test_login_nonexistent_user(client, app):
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "nobody", "password": "x"})
    assert resp.status_code == 401


# ── Logout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_logout_success(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/logout", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json()["message"] == "Successfully logged out"


def test_logout_unauthenticated(client, app):
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/logout")
    assert resp.status_code == 401


# ── Validate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_validate_token(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/validate", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["is_valid"] is True
    assert data["user_id"] == test_user.id


def test_validate_no_token(client, app):
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/validate")
    assert resp.status_code == 401


# ── Me ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_me(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/me", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["username"] == "testuser"
    assert data["email"] == "test@example.com"
    assert data["name"] == "Test User"


# ── Refresh ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_refresh_token(client, test_user, auth_header):
    # First get a token via login
    login_resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "password123"})
    token = login_resp.json()["access_token"]
    # Use it to refresh
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/refresh", json={"refresh_token": token})
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["access_token"]
    assert data["user_id"] == test_user.id


def test_refresh_invalid_token(client, app):
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/refresh", json={"refresh_token": "bad.token.here"})
    assert resp.status_code == 401

from datetime import datetime
from tests.conftest import TestingSessionLocal
from database.models import IDMSData, APIUsage


def _seed_idms(n=3):
    """Insert sample IDMS rows."""
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        session.add(IDMSData(column_1=f"val{i}", column_2=f"data{i}"))
    session.commit()
    session.close()


def _seed_api_usage(pages=("auth", "dashboard", "settings"), count_each=2):
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    for page in pages:
        for _ in range(count_each):
            session.add(APIUsage(
                endpoint=f"/api/{page}/test",
                method="GET",
                page=page,
                response_status=200,
                response_time_ms=10,
                timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
            ))
    session.commit()
    session.close()


# ── IDMS Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_idms_data_empty(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/idms-data", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["data"] == []
    assert data["total"] == 0


def test_idms_data_with_rows(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_idms(3)
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/idms-data", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["total"] == 3
    assert data["data"][0]["column_1"] == "val1"


def test_idms_data_unauthenticated(client, app):
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/idms-data")
    assert resp.status_code == 401


# ── API Usage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_api_usage_empty(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/api-usage", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["total_calls"] == 0


def test_api_usage_with_data(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_api_usage()
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/api-usage", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json()["total_calls"] == 6


def test_api_usage_total(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_api_usage(count_each=5)
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/api-usage/total", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json()["total_calls"] == 15


# ── API Usage Breakdown ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_api_usage_breakdown(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_api_usage(pages=("auth", "dashboard"), count_each=3)
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/api-usage/breakdown", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["total_calls"] == 6
    pages = {item["page"] for item in data["breakdown"]}
    assert "auth" in pages
    assert "dashboard" in pages
    for item in data["breakdown"]:
        assert item["percentage"] == 50.0


def test_api_usage_breakdown_unauthenticated(client, app):
    resp = client.get("/api/dashboard/api-usage/breakdown")
    assert resp.status_code == 401
"}

from tests.conftest import TestingSessionLocal
from database.models import AuditLog
from datetime import datetime


def _seed_audit_logs(user_id, n=5):
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    for i in range(n):
        session.add(AuditLog(
            user_id=user_id,
            action="login",
            description=f"Test action {i}",
            timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
        ))
    session.commit()
    session.close()


# ── List ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_list_audit_logs_empty(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.get("/api/audit/", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["data"] == []
    assert data["total"] == 0
    assert data["page"] == 1


def test_list_audit_logs_with_data(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_audit_logs(test_user.id, 5)
    resp = client.get("/api/audit/", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["total"] == 5
    assert len(data["data"]) == 5


def test_list_audit_logs_pagination(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_audit_logs(test_user.id, 25)
    resp = client.get("/api/audit/?page=1&page_size=10", headers=auth_header)
    data = resp.json()
    assert len(data["data"]) == 10
    assert data["total"] == 25
    assert data["total_pages"] == 3

    resp2 = client.get("/api/audit/?page=3&page_size=10", headers=auth_header)
    assert len(resp2.json()["data"]) == 5


def test_list_audit_logs_unauthenticated(client, app):
    resp = client.get("/api/audit/")
    assert resp.status_code == 401


# ── Detail ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_audit_log_detail(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_audit_logs(test_user.id, 1)
    # Fetch list to get an ID
    logs = client.get("/api/audit/", headers=auth_header).json()["data"]
    log_id = logs[0]["id"]

    resp = client.get(f"/api/audit/{log_id}", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    detail = resp.json()
    assert detail["id"] == log_id
    assert detail["username"] == "testuser"
    assert detail["user_name"] == "Test User"


def test_audit_log_detail_not_found(client, test_user, auth_header):
    resp = client.get("/api/audit/99999", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 404


# ── Access control ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_audit_log_detail_access_denied(client, test_user, second_user, auth_header):
    """User cannot view another user's audit log entry."""
    _seed_audit_logs(second_user.id, 1)
    session = TestingSessionLocal()
    log = session.query(AuditLog).filter(AuditLog.user_id == second_user.id).first()
    log_id = log.id
    session.close()

    resp = client.get(f"/api/audit/{log_id}", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 403


def test_user_audit_logs_access_denied(client, test_user, second_user, auth_header):
    """User cannot list another user's audit logs."""
    resp = client.get(f"/api/audit/user/{second_user.id}", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 403


def test_user_audit_logs_own(client, test_user, auth_header):
    _seed_audit_logs(test_user.id, 3)
    resp = client.get(f"/api/audit/user/{test_user.id}", headers=auth_header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json()["total"] == 3
"}

import pytest
from fastapi import HTTPException

from services.auth_service import (
    get_password_hash,
    verify_password,
    create_access_token,
    verify_token,
    authenticate_user,
    get_user_by_username,
    get_user_by_id,
)
from services.audit_service import (
    create_audit_log,
    get_audit_logs,
    get_audit_log_by_id,
    log_login,
    log_logout,
    log_profile_update,
    log_password_change,
)


# ── Password hashing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_hash_and_verify():
    hashed = get_password_hash("secret")
    assert verify_password("secret", hashed)
    assert not verify_password("wrong", hashed)


# ── JWT tokens ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_create_and_verify_token():
    token = create_access_token(data={"sub": "42", "username": "alice"})
    payload = verify_token(token)
    assert payload["sub"] == "42"
    assert payload["username"] == "alice"


def test_verify_invalid_token():
    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc_info:
        verify_token("not.a.valid.token")
    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 401


# ── User lookup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_authenticate_user_success(db, test_user):
    user = authenticate_user(db, "testuser", "password123")
    assert user is not None
    assert user.username == "testuser"


def test_authenticate_user_wrong_password(db, test_user):
    assert authenticate_user(db, "testuser", "wrong") is None


def test_authenticate_user_missing(db):
    assert authenticate_user(db, "ghost", "x") is None


def test_get_user_by_username(db, test_user):
    user = get_user_by_username(db, "testuser")
    assert user is not None
    assert user.id == test_user.id


def test_get_user_by_id(db, test_user):
    user = get_user_by_id(db, test_user.id)
    assert user is not None
    assert user.username == "testuser"


def test_get_user_by_id_missing(db):
    assert get_user_by_id(db, 99999) is None


# ── Audit logging ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_create_audit_log(db, test_user):
    entry = create_audit_log(db, user_id=test_user.id, action="test", description="unit test")
    assert entry.id is not None
    assert entry.action == "test"


def test_get_audit_logs_pagination(db, test_user):
    for _ in range(15):
        create_audit_log(db, user_id=test_user.id, action="login")
    result = get_audit_logs(db, user_id=test_user.id, page=1, page_size=10)
    assert result["total"] == 15
    assert len(result["data"]) == 10
    assert result["total_pages"] == 2


def test_get_audit_log_by_id(db, test_user):
    entry = create_audit_log(db, user_id=test_user.id, action="x")
    found = get_audit_log_by_id(db, entry.id)
    assert found is not None
    assert found.action == "x"


def test_log_login(db, test_user):
    entry = log_login(db, test_user.id, "127.0.0.1", "pytest")
    assert entry.action == "login"
    assert entry.ip_address == "127.0.0.1"


def test_log_logout(db, test_user):
    entry = log_logout(db, test_user.id, "127.0.0.1", "pytest")
    assert entry.action == "logout"


def test_log_profile_update(db, test_user):
    entry = log_profile_update(db, test_user.id, ["name", "email"])
    assert entry.action == "profile_update"
    assert "name" in entry.details


def test_log_password_change(db, test_user):
    entry = log_password_change(db, test_user.id)
    assert entry.action == "password_change"
"}

    """Blacklisted JWT tokens (invalidated on logout)"""
    __tablename__ = "blacklisted_tokens"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    token = Column(String(500), unique=True, index=True, nullable=False)
    blacklisted_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    expires_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<BlacklistedToken(id={self.id})>"


class

is_token_blacklisted(db: Session, token: str) -> bool:
    """Check whether a token has been blacklisted (e.g. after logout)."""
    return db.query(BlacklistedToken).filter(BlacklistedToken.token == token).first() is not None


def blacklist_token(db: Session, token: str) -> None:
    """Add a token to the blacklist so it can no longer be used."""

    entry = BlacklistedToken(token=token, expires_at=expires_at)

# ── Token Blacklisting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_logout_blacklists_token(client, test_user):
    """After logout the same token should be rejected."""
    login_resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "password123"})
    token = login_resp.json()["access_token"]
    header = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    # Logout should succeed
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/logout", headers=header)
    assert resp.status_code == 200

    # Subsequent requests with the same token should be rejected
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/me", headers=header)
    assert resp.status_code == 401
    assert "revoked" in resp.json()["detail"].lower()


def test_blacklisted_token_cannot_validate(client, test_user):
    login_resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "password123"})
    token = login_resp.json()["access_token"]
    header = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    client.post("/api/auth/logout", headers=header)
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/validate", headers=header)
    assert resp.status_code == 401


def test_refresh_blacklists_old_token(client, test_user):
    """After refreshing, the old token should be blacklisted."""
    login_resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "password123"})
    old_token = login_resp.json()["access_token"]

    refresh_resp = client.post("/api/auth/refresh", json={"refresh_token": old_token})
    assert refresh_resp.status_code == 200
    new_token = refresh_resp.json()["access_token"]

    # Old token should be rejected
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/me", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {old_token}"})
    assert resp.status_code == 401

    # New token should work
    resp = client.get("/api/auth/me", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {new_token}"})
    assert resp.status_code == 200


def test_refresh_blacklisted_token_rejected(client, test_user):
    """Cannot refresh a token that was already blacklisted."""
    login_resp = client.post("/api/auth/login", json={"username": "testuser", "password": "password123"})
    token = login_resp.json()["access_token"]

    # Logout blacklists the token
    client.post("/api/auth/logout", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})

    # Trying to refresh with the blacklisted token should fail
    resp = client.post("/api/auth/refresh", json={"refresh_token": token})
    assert resp.status_code == 401
